courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Exploring Health Policy and Health Systems
courses.description: This course is designed to provide students with an opportunity to explore health policy issues, learn about health systems, and introduce them to the field of health policy and management.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Global Health in Context - Historical Trajectories and Economic Policy
courses.description: This course introduces global health in context, covering foundational frameworks, economic and policy approaches, and the organization of health systems worldwide. Students explore service delivery challenges in low- and middle-income countries--including quality improvement, digital health, and pharmaceuticals--and examine cross-cutting issues such as noncommunicable diseases, climate change, and displacement.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: The U.S. Health System
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the U.S. health care system, including how the system is structured and financed and the delivery of health care services. Students will explore the performance of the system in terms of population health, quality, access, cost and equity, and approaches to strengthening health system performance. This course is intended for students who are pursuing a Business of Health minor and other juniors and seniors who are not pursuing a Health Policy and Management major.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Special Topics in HPM
courses.description: Special topics course for health policy and management undergraduate students.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Community and Public Health Security: Disasters, Terrorism, and Emergency Management
courses.description: This course examines systems for emergency management at federal, state, and local levels. The roles of emergency management, health services, and public health in disaster management are also reviewed. Every other week, evening online sessions required with instructors.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Emergency Management I: Analytic Methods
courses.description: Introduction of analytical tools to assess, evaluate, map, and investigate disasters (including biological outbreaks). These tools will be used to improve planning and evaluation of disaster management programs. Every other week, evening online sessions required with instructors.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Emergency Management II: Disaster Management
courses.description: Explores issues of preparedness, response, recovery, mitigation, and research in disaster management. Students will participate in evacuation decision making, volunteer management, and the development of a disaster exercise. Every other week, evening online sessions required with instructors.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Program Evaluation
courses.description: Concepts and methods of the program evaluation paradigm as applied in health administration.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Readings in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Directed readings or research. Written reports are required.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: HPM BSPH Professional Development Seminar
courses.description: This course exposes students to different career paths in the field of Health Policy and Management and helps students develop knowledge and skills needed to effectively compete for internships and post-graduation jobs. HPM BSPH majors only. Previously offered as HPM 301.

source.text: HPM 501. | 1 Credits. | Pre- or corequisite, HPM 502 .

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to the U.S. Health System I
courses.description: HPM 502 and 503 provide an overview of the United States health system. HPM 502 examines the performance, organization, management, and financing of the U.S. health system and the resources required to provide health services. Previously offered as HPM 350.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to the U.S. Health System II
courses.description: HPM 503 , in conjunction with HPM 502 , provides an overview of the United States health system. HPM 503 examines the delivery of health services and approaches to strengthening the performance of the U.S. health system. HPM BSPH Majors Only. Previously offered as HPM 352.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to Health Law and Ethics
courses.description: An introduction to law and ethics in public health and healthcare organizations. HPM BSPH Majors Only. Previously offered as HPM 310.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to Strategic Planning and Marketing in Health Care
courses.description: An introduction to the development and implementation of strategic planning and marketing processes in health care organizations. Previously offered as HPM 320.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to Health Organization Leadership, Management, and Behavior
courses.description: Students develop skills in leadership and management and apply these skills to public health and health care cases and a team-based community project. Previously offered as HPM 330.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Foundations of Health Care Financial Management
courses.description: Basic methods and techniques in financial management of health care programs, including financial statement analysis, cost determination and allocation, pricing of services, and budgeting. Previously offered as HPM 340.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Analytics in Health Systems
courses.description: This course examines applications of analytical techniques in health systems. Emphasis is on model formulation and computer solution of decision models using various analytical tools in Excel. Previously offered as HPM 341.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Politics, Public Health, and Health Policy
courses.description: This course explores the politics of public health and health care policy in the United States, with a focus on current issues and controversies. Previously offered as HPM 351.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Internship in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: A 320-hour internship in a health-related organization. The internship provides students an opportunity to apply the knowledge and skills they are learning in the classroom, gain valuable experience and explore career interests. Previously offered as HPM 393. Restricted to HPM B.S.P.H. students.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 12 total credits. 6 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to Health Policy and Management
courses.description: This course provides an overview of the United States health care system. Students will explore the system's organization, financing, management, resources, and performance. For each topic, they will analyze relevant legislation and discuss current issues. Students will develop skills in policy research and analysis, health care system evaluation, and basic financial literacy.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Issues in Health Care
courses.description: Lectures on current topics in health care.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Concurrent Practice
courses.description: Permission of the program director. Supervised activities in an approved health organization, to include one or more specific projects, approved by HPM faculty member and directed by an approved preceptor/mentor in the organization.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Practice Application Journaling I
courses.description: This course is the first of six field-based Journal Practica in which students monitor their learning processes, identify where knowledge and skills learned in courses are helpful and relevant to areas of their professional responsibility, and apply that knowledge and those skills to actual work situations.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 1 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 1 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.title: Practice Application Journaling VI
courses.description: This course is the sixth and final of six field-based journal practica in which students monitor their learning processes, identify where knowledge and skills learned in courses are helpful and relevant to areas of their professional responsibility, and apply that knowledge and those skills to actual work situations.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 1 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Implementing Health Informatics Initiatives
courses.description: Focuses on implementing informatics programs and projects in health organizations. Informatics initiatives aim to facilitate effective information use for the purpose of improving the quality of health services and/or efficiency of processes. Therefore, these initiatives have implications for various stakeholder groups, including consumers, practitioners, administrators, and policy makers.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: International Humanitarian Crises and Emergencies
courses.description: Introduction to humanitarian crises and emergencies, those who respond to them, interventions and management including evaluation. These tools will be used in recognizing, improving planning and evaluation of international crises response programs. Every other week, evening online sessions are required with instructors. This course meets requirements to serve as a graduate and undergraduate elective. Permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: IHI Course in Healthcare Quality Improvement
courses.description: The IHI Certificate demonstrates an investment in further education and a strong knowledge base in quality improvement. Upon completion of this course, students will have met the requirements for the IHI Open School Certificate and participated in two in-person sessions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: International and Comparative Health Systems
courses.description: Methods of comparing health systems, examinations of related national health systems, and analysis of related high prevalence health issues.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Global Health Law & Policy
courses.description: Coursework will focus on public policy approaches to global health, employing interdisciplinary methodologies to understand selected public health policies, programs, and interventions. For students who have a basic understanding of public health. Course previously offered as PLCY/HPM 565.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Global Health and Human Rights
courses.description: Course focuses on rights-based approaches to health, applying a human rights perspective to selected public health policies, programs, and interventions. Students will apply a formalistic human rights framework to critical public health issues, exploring human rights as both a safeguard against harm and a catalyst for health promotion. Course previously offered as PLCY 570/HPM 571.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Globalization and Health
courses.description: Globalization--its economic, environmental, political, technological, institutional, and sociocultural dimensions--historically and currently contributes to beneficial and adverse effects on population, community, and family and individual health.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Statistical Methods for Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Introduction to statistical analysis for healthcare settings using an Excel framework. Topics include variable types, sampling, probability distributions, descriptive statistics, hypothesis testing, categorical data analysis, ANOVA, and introduction to regression methods. Previously offered as HPM 470.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Special Topics in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Special topics course for health policy and management undergraduate students.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Honors Research I
courses.description: Students design a research project, known as the Honors Thesis. Students write a research proposal and complete an IRB application toward partial completion of the thesis. Requires a UNC-approved cumulative GPA by the end of the junior year and permission of the instructor.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Honors Research II
courses.description: Students complete, write up and present the Honors Thesis research project that they designed in HPM 691H . Requires having maintained the UNC-approved cumulative GPA by the end of the senior fall semester and permission of the instructor.

source.text: HPM 692H. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, HPM 691H and 350. | RESEARCH.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Research in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: This course is for health policy and management undergraduate or graduate students who wish to pursue applied research or practice opportunities with healthcare organizations under the supervision of a faculty member in the Department of Health Policy and Management.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 12 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Policy and Management BSPH Capstone
courses.description: The capstone course serves as a culminating experience for students in the BSPH program in Health Policy and Management. Students integrate and apply the knowledge and skills they have learned across the program. Students work in teams to complete a major project with a local organization -- such as a hospital, health system, governmental health department, non-profit, or global health organization. Restricted to HPM B.S.P.H. students.

source.text: HPM 697. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, HPM 330 and HPM 350. | RESEARCH.

courses.title: Healthcare Management Skills Development Workshop I
courses.description: This course is the first of two workshops for students in the Executive Master's Program. These workshops are designed to provide students exposure to key cross cutting skills that will be used in the program. These skills also are essential for effective healthcare management.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Healthcare Management Skills Development Workshop II
courses.description: This course is the second of two workshops for students in the Executive Master's Program. These workshops are designed to provide students exposure to key cross cutting skills that will be used in the program. These skills also are essential for effective healthcare management.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Law
courses.description: An introduction to law and the legal system as it relates to the delivery and financing of health care.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Hospital Functions and Operations
courses.description: This course provides exposure to the knowledge and skills required to solve the most pressing operational problems found across departments within today's complex health care institutions.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Advanced Spreadsheet Modeling for Business
courses.description: This course focuses on using advanced features of Microsoft Excel to create efficient spreadsheet models of common and complex business problems. It challenges students to use critical thinking and analysis to find effective solutions to real-life situations.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Economics for Policy and Management
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for nonmajors. Provides training in the theory of health economics and applies this theory to important issues in health policy and management.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Mental Health Services Research and Policy
courses.description: This course is an introduction to mental health services research and policy. Topics include the financing of mental health services, supply of services, quality measures, assessing need, and barriers to care. The course includes seminar presentations by local and nationally recognized experts in mental health services research and discussion sessions.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Management of Human Resources in Health Organizations
courses.description: Emphasis is on clarifying concepts of human resources management and identifying the importance of human resources in health organizations.

Students develop practical skills such as assessing the internal and external environment, competitor analysis, and evaluating strategic alternatives in different health care settings. It also explores the role the governing board plays in strategy development and management.

courses.description: This course provides an introduction and overview to leadership, management, human resources and organizational behavior, with the goal of aligning these with the organization's strategy and mission. The course integrates theory with practice through readings, lectures, written assignments, and guest presentations from different organizational perspectives. Assessment, practice and development of leadership, managerial and organizational skills will be accomplished through team exercises and small group work.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Leadership and Workforce Management Strategies
courses.description: This course provides an introduction and overview of leadership, management, workforce challenges, and organizational behavior. The course emphasizes the importance of aligning management practices with the organization's mission and goals. The course integrates theory with practice through readings, lectures, written assignments, experiential exercises, and guest presentations. Assessment, practice and development of leadership, managerial and organizational skills are accomplished through team exercises, self and peer assessments, and small group work.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Approaches to Business Plan Development
courses.description: Approaches to Business Plan Development ('Capstone Prep') is a one-credit course to introduce and jumpstart the Spring Semester Capstone business plan process necessary for HPM 735 .

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Advanced Concepts and Applications in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Required preparation, completion of master's core (can be concurrent). Restricted to HPM graduate students. Integrating and building upon the HPM master's core, this comprehensive course focuses on organization policymaking and administration from the perspective of the CEO and top management.

courses.title: Health Care Financial Accounting
courses.description: This introduces concepts of financial accounting to the non-accountant user of financial information. Basic accounting transactions, financial report preparation, concepts of accrual vs. cash accounting, not-for-profit health care accounting, and the analysis of health care organization financial reports.

courses.description: Permission of the instructor for non-MHA majors. Covers selected topics in managerial accounting applied to health care.

courses.description: Basic financial management concepts, including time value analysis, financial risk and required return, long-term debt financing, equity financing and securities markets, capital structure and the cost of capital, the basics of capital budgeting, project risk analysis, revenue cycle and current accounts management, and financial condition analysis.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Care Reimbursement
courses.description: This online course in health care reimbursement is designed to provide students with relevant and current information about health care reimbursement methods and the complexities around it. After completion of the course, students should have an operational knowledge of health care reimbursement theory and practice.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Care Finance II
courses.description: Focuses on capital allocation, financial condition analysis and forecasting, and other topics. Course is the conclusion to a five-course sequence in healthcare financial management. Each builds on the prior course with the intent of providing a comprehensive foundation in the concepts and practice of healthcare financial management.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Financial Management and Analysis for Public and Nonprofit Entities
courses.description: This course teaches financial concepts for students seeking leadership roles in the non-profit and government sector, including business planning, budgeting, accounting, performance management, and resource blending and braiding. Students will develop a business plan and learn key strategies and evaluation tools.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to Financial and Managerial Accounting for Healthcare Organizations
courses.description: Focuses on learning and applying key financial and managerial accounting tools and concepts to healthcare problems. Provides a broad introduction to key concepts, issues, tools, and vocabulary useful for policymakers and administrators. Topics include: reading and analyzing healthcare financial statements, recording transactions, budgeting, full costing, incremental costing, and responsibility accounting.

courses.title: Health Care Finance

The course includes the healthcare environment, basic financial management concepts, capital acquisition, cost of capital and capital structure, and capital allocation. After completion of the course, students should be able to apply financial management concepts in real world healthcare settings.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Economic Principles, Health Insurance & Behavioral Economics in Health
courses.description: This course provides students with an opportunity to investigate topics of healthcare policy and insurance from a finance and economics perspective. The course covers contemporary health policy topics in great depth and with a focus on economic and financial analysis as a tool to evaluate healthcare policies and proposed new legislation.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Data Visualization
courses.description: Introduction to data visualization principles and tools for business professionals. Topics include cognitive processing of visual information, best practices in data visualization, effective data storytelling, data acquisition and preparation, and designing data visualizations using Tableau Desktop software.

courses.title: Health Care in the United States: Structure and Policy
courses.description: This core course is designed to provide students with an overview of the structure, systems, and policies of health care delivery in the United States. The goal is to increase students' knowledge and abilities to analyze and address health care issues from both management and policy perspectives.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Care in the United States Structure and Policy
courses.description: This core course is designed to provide students with an overview of the structure, systems, and policies of health care delivery in the United States. The goal is to increase students' knowledge and abilities to analyze and address health care issues from both management and policy perspectives.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Systems and Service Delivery in the Global South
courses.description: This graduate course offers public health students an in-depth exploration of key components of health service delivery in the Global South, focusing on complex challenges and innovative solutions for optimizing healthcare in these settings. The course covers various health domains, including sexual and reproductive health, mental health, infectious diseases, non-communicable diseases, and rural health. Additionally, students will delve into the historical evolution of Global Health, tracing its progression from colonial medicine to international health and, finally, contemporary global health, using an anticolonial framework to examine these transitions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Conceptualizing & Measuring Access to Healthcare
courses.description: This course addresses theoretical and applied approaches to measuring health care access in public health and health services research. Drawing principally from health and medical geography, linking foundational concepts and methods addressing access with health economics and health services research more broadly. Students explore spatial approaches to health and healthcare in place. This course will include reading responses, GIS lab exercises, and a research project addressing health care access. Prior exposure to statistical methods preferred.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Reform: Political Dynamics and Policy Dilemmas
courses.description: This course focuses on the political and policy dynamics of health care reform. We explore why health reform is so difficult to achieve in the U.S., lessons from past reform successes and failures, the dilemmas confronting public and private insurers from rising health care costs, the elusive pursuit of universal health insurance, and lessons from other countries. Our goal is to understand how politics shape health policymaking, the contemporary state of health reform, and possible futures for American health policy, from consumer-driven health care to Medicare for All.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Underserved Populations and Health Reform
courses.description: This course gives students a greater understanding of programs available to serve underserved populations, and how the ACA (or any replacement) will impact on care provided to underserved populations. The course is designed to help students think critically about the impact of policy changes on different populations.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Policy Analysis and Advocacy for Health Leaders
courses.description: This course will provide students with a hands-on opportunity to learn about the health policy development process. Students will gain an understanding of the different ways in which health policy is made through the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of government, as well as the role of the media and advocates/stakeholder groups in shaping health policy. Students will also gain practical experience designing and implementing a campaign aimed at changing health policy.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Healthcare Quality and Information Management
courses.description: Integrates essential methods and principles in healthcare quality and information management. Emphasis on use of information to measure and improve quality. Will include presentations, individual/group projects, exercises, and group discussion.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Quality of Care
courses.description: The quality of health care in the US has garnered significant attention. This course will examine 1) the current state of the quality of care in the US, 2) approaches to assess quality of care, and 3) strategies that have been implemented or proposed to improve the quality of care.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Caregiving: Research, Practice, & Policy
courses.description: Informal or family caregivers support a family member or friend with a serious health problem, disability, or illness. Caregiving is an essential part of our society and infrastructure worldwide. Understanding informal care within the context of both healthcare delivery and the community is critical for future professionals in healthcare, social services, and health policy. This course will provide an overview of caregiving in the U.S. and globally, models of caregiving, research methods, and caregiving policies.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Cancer Prevention and Control Seminar
courses.description: An interdisciplinary overview of cancer prevention and control. Emphasis on projects and activities from perspectives of epidemiology, health behavior and education, and health policy and management. Appropriate research design and methodologies are covered.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Improving Healthcare Quality for All: Applications in Research, Policy, and Practice
courses.description: This graduate-level course examines contemporary perspectives on defining, measuring, and advancing healthcare quality for all populations across research, policy, and practice contexts. The course emphasizes critical appraisal of evidence, the role of policy and governance, and the translation of research findings into practical strategies for enhancing care delivery. Students will examine conceptual frameworks, methodological approaches, and implementation strategies used to assess and improve upon healthcare quality for all populations. A central component of the course is a semester-long culminating project in which students synthesize course concepts to design, assess, or propose an initiative to improve healthcare quality for all.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Implementation Science in Health
courses.description: This course introduces the concepts, theories, and methods of disseminating and implementing evidence-based health, behavioral health, and social service interventions. The course also examines the methods for conducting rigorous research on dissemination and implementation.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Cancer Outcomes Research Seminar
courses.description: The Cancer Outcomes Research Program (CORP) offers a weekly seminar for faculty, students, and fellows/trainees interested in multidisciplinary cancer outcomes research. Guest speakers' topics include Quality of Care, Patient-reported Outcomes (PROs), Comparative Effectiveness, Health Informatics, Cancer Disparities, Decision Making, Dissemination/Implementation, and Health Economics, as related to cancer outcomes.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Operations Research for Healthcare Systems
courses.description: Review of the systems analysis process in healthcare systems. Deterministic and random models, mathematical programming, queueing, simulation, forecasting, and measurement. Emphasis on model formulation and computer solution of decision models.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Techniques for the Economic Evaluation of Health Care
courses.description: This course provides an investigation of the theory, methods, and application of economic evaluation to health care. Topics include methods used to structure an economic evaluation, measure and summarize health outcomes and estimate their value to patients or to the public, and identify resources used and estimate their costs.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to Program Evaluation in Public Health and Health Care Settings
courses.description: This course is a three-credit hour introduction to program evaluation in public health and health care settings. We discuss key concepts in planning, conducting, reporting, and utilizing evaluations. Through a semester-long project students develop a viable program evaluation design for a real-world program.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Healthcare Quality and Information Management
courses.description: The HPM 776 / 777 and 776 /778 course sequences integrate essential methods and principles in healthcare quality and information management, emphasizing use of information to measure and improve quality.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Information and Quality Applications
courses.description: The HPM 776 / 777 and 776 /778 course sequences integrate essential methods and principles in healthcare quality and information management, emphasizing use of information to measure and improve quality.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Operations Research for Healthcare Systems
courses.description: Healthcare administrators face a range of decisions: some strategic, some financial, others operational. Through your program of study, you are developing analytical and conceptual skills that will help you to make better decisions when the time comes.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 8 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Pharmaceutical Health Policy
courses.description: Overview of the pharmaceutical industry including organization, financing, major regulations, drug development, and ethical considerations. Topics will give a real-world perspective from professionals in the pharmaceutical industry. Students will debate and discuss some controversial topics related to pharmaceuticals and public health including patient safety, data integrity, financial conflicts of interest, and pricing. These topics will introduce students to careers in the pharmaceutical industry and provide a relevant background for careers in public policy or research.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Advanced Decision Modeling
courses.description: This course covers advanced decision modeling methods in health care, including probabilistic sensitivity and value of information analysis, economic evaluation using clinical trial data, and discrete event simulation and agent-based/system dynamics modeling techniques. The course teaches analytical techniques and interpretation as well as state-of-the-art best practices.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Master's Paper Development
courses.description: Second-year M.S.P.H. students in HPM only. Course supports the year-long master's paper process. Broad topics related to the development and management of a research project are covered. The Master's Paper Proposal Defense at the end of the Fall Semester, and the Final Master's Paper, as approved by the student's First and Second Readers at the end of the Spring Semester, are critical steps to meet the UNC Graduate School's requirements for graduation. M.S.P.H. students only.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Advanced Health Policy Analysis and Advocacy
courses.description: This class will provide students with an opportunity to learn about the health policy analysis and advocacy processes in the United States. Students will gain an understanding of the different ways in which health policies are made at the legislative, regulatory, and judicial systems. Students will also learn how to identify and analyze different policy options to address health problems, conduct a stakeholders' analysis, and design an advocacy campaign.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Value Based Payment Policy
courses.description: This course will cover value based models in health care, including accountable care organizations, bundled payments, patient centered medical home models, risk-based contracts, and other related programs. We will cover the goals of these models, what we mean by "value" in health care, how payment arrangements work practically, evidence on the effectiveness of these models for improving quality and efficiency in health care, and the policies addressing value-based payment.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Clinical Transformations
courses.description: This course seeks to expose students to an array of topics around health care clinical transformation through presentations and discussion with guest speakers from a range of stakeholders, including frontline providers, leaders at health care organizations, and state policymakers.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Policy and Management Internship
courses.description: Restricted to HPM majors. Supervised field experience in approved health agencies. (Internship fee: $450.)
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Patient-Reported Outcomes Measurement and Application in Healthcare Research and Practice
courses.description: Patient-reported outcomes (PROs) include measures of health status, quality of life, and satisfaction with healthcare. This course provides an overview of the PRO measurement and research field, and discusses how to design and evaluate a PRO measure and best practices for integrating PRO in clinical research and healthcare settings.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 6 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Systems Thinking & Collective Impact
courses.description: This course is designed to help you become familiar with and thoughtfully apply a variety of practical, structured, systems thinking approaches to improve population health by changing aspects of care, service delivery systems, policy, and/or environments in which we live and work. We'll use these methods to both understand individuals' experiences as the foundation for driving change as well as to "zoom out" and see the broader system around a population health challenge.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Leadership in Public Health Law and Ethics
courses.description: Course is designed to provide learners with an introduction and overview of critical issues relating to law, ethics, and public health. DrPH students only.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Graduate Health Economics Seminar
courses.description: Permission of the instructor. Discussion of recent papers in health economics. Students must have solid knowledge of graduate microeconomics theory and econometrics.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 3 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Organizational Leadership Theory and Practice
courses.description: This introductory course will provide an overview of the theoretical framework for the practice of leadership in organizations leading to the application of theory and best practices in your leadership practice. We will also focus on specific leadership topics such as strategic leadership, systems thinking, team leadership, change management and developing others. We believe that you can learn about leadership in a course such as ours, but you can only really learn leadership by practicing it.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Global Health Diplomacy
courses.description: This course describes and analyzes global health diplomacy. The course will include descriptions of the historical underpinnings of global health diplomacy, global health governance, the evolution of global health diplomacy and its effects on global health governance and selected contemporary issues. This course will discuss how countries across the globe tackle public health issues through cooperation, trust, within established mechanisms and emerging partnerships, to achieve health outcomes beyond national interests.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Translational Health Disparities: Research, Practice & Policy
courses.description: This course will focus on the concepts, principles, methods, and applications of health disparities science, practice, and policy. It will integrate principles and practice of community engagement. Experts from diverse disciplines will give lectures on health disparities research, practice, and policy. Student teams will work on real life case studies.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Population Perspectives for Health and the Research Process
courses.description: This course examines historical and contemporary population health and public health perspectives. These perspectives shape the politics and policy making that affect global health. The practical goal is to help the entering DrPH student develop a grounding for further exploration of topics that may evolve into a dissertation.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Seminar in Teaching Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Problems and processes of teaching health policy and management, including supervised practicum experience.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Policy Seminar in Health Policy and Management
courses.description: Seminar on policy issues in health policy and management.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Advanced Research Seminar in HPM
courses.description: This seminar will develop core competencies through a: (1) journal club to develop competencies in research design and expose students to diverse content and methodologies; and (2) professional development series.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Principles of Health Policy Research Methods
courses.description: First course in the department's sequence in empirical analysis. Covers principles of statistical inference, univariate and bivariate analysis, statistical software applications, and mathematical concepts necessary for linear regression and further topics.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Introduction to Applied Methods in Health Services Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. Familiarity with Stata or R. This course is the first in a sequence of empirical methods courses focused on causal inference. We will begin with linear regression models (i.e., ordinary least squares) and extend to nonlinear, matching, and propensity score approaches. For each approach, the course explores how to test each of the underlying assumptions and how to correct the model when the assumptions fail. We will use Stata and R software.

source.text: HPM 881. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisite, BIOS 600 or HPM 880 .

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Advanced Methodology in Health Services Research
courses.description: Permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites. Students will apply models and statistical techniques to original health services research; understand major techniques used to estimate causal relationships in quasi-experimental designs, including panel data and simultaneous equations models; and gain intuition and skills about the art of econometrics, including techniques for using complex survey data and handling missing data.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Applied Methods in Health Services Research
courses.description: This course provides a practical introduction to experimental methods and machine learning techniques with direct applications in health services research. Students will engage in hands-on activities to build practical skills in designing and analyzing experiments -- both small and large scale -- to address causal questions in health services. Additionally, students will apply supervised machine learning approaches to tackle prediction problems relevant to health services research.
courses.requisites_raw: Prerequisites, HPM 881 and 882; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

items.text: permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites

source.text: HPM 883. | 3 Credits. | Prerequisites, HPM 881 and 882 ; permission of the instructor for students lacking the prerequisites.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Overview of Health Services Research/Health Policy
courses.description: Pre-doctoral standing or permission of the instructor. This course provides an overview of the field of health services research and health policy. It introduces basic components of the research process, including literature synthesis, development of a research question and hypothesis, and use of conceptual models to guide research questions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Health Services/Health Policy Research Methods
courses.description: This course explores how to develop answerable, policy-relevant, ethical research questions; operationalize questions with actionable specific aims' and identify optimal research design for answering a particular question. It introduces primary data collection methods (e.g., interviews, focus groups, surveys) and secondary data sources (e.g., administrative claims, medical, records).

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Qualitative and Mixed Methods Designs
courses.description: This course focuses on the application of qualitative and mixed methods designs that are relevant to health services and health policy researchers.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Special Topics in HPM
courses.description: Course reserved for special topics in HPM for graduate-level students only.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics; 3 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Public Health Informatics Practicum
courses.description: Course will help students: conduct research, develop public health informatics tools/projects, and further develop professional skills and knowledge essential in the public health informatics field. Students will participate in weekly (2 hr) informatics discussions with practicum preceptors and have an opportunity to meet and interact with successful health informatics professionals.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Leadership in Health Informatics
courses.description: The course offers an overview of health informatics for DrPH students in leadership roles. The course will focus on leading informatics savvy organizations by use of case studies discussed by outside experts as well as students and faculty. The course will rely on active class discussion.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 4 total credits. 4 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Dissertation Planning and Preparation
courses.description: Part of a sequence to guide students in planning, development, and implementation of Dr.P.H. dissertations. Designed to prepare students to identify appropriate research topics, plan the approach, organize, and write.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Dissertation Planning and Preparation III
courses.description: The purpose of this course is to build on students' progress on work initiated in HPM 946 and continue to guide students through the steps necessary to complete a dissertation proposal. In collaboration with faculty, learners will assess the current state of their proposals and complete revisions and additional refinements, culminating in dissertations that are ready to be defended by fall of the third year in the program.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Literature Reviews and Appraisal
courses.description: This course is the second in a sequence of courses in research design and methods in the executive Dr.P.H. program. The course explores the nature and process of scientific inquiry in the field of public health, establishing a foundation for methodological exploration, and focusing on the process of developing researchable questions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Essentials of Practice Based Research
courses.description: Designed to provide Dr.P.H. students with grounding in basic quantitative and qualitative research techniques used in health services research. Topics include types of research designs, measurement scales and coding nomenclatures, analytical techniques for quantitative data, research techniques for primary data collection, research opportunities with secondary data, and qualitative research methods.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Fundamentals of Research Methods and Analysis
courses.description: This course will provide students with "hands-on" experience in qualitative, quantitative, and policy analytical techniques. DrPH students only.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Crisis Leadership
courses.description: Offered exclusively to students in the Executive DrPH program, this course exposes students to the theoretical and practical aspects of organizational crises and prepares them to lead effectively in the midst of crisis situations.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit. 2 total credits. 2 total completions.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Financial Leadership
courses.description: Dr.P.H. students only. Understand the major concepts of financial oversight, including budgeting, financial statement analysis, internal controls, governance, and the Sarbanes-Oxley Act, and be able to apply them to all organizations, whether public, private, non-profit, or governmental. Utilizing both individual and team-based learning.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Strategic Planning for Public and Non-Profit Organizations
courses.description: The purpose of this class is to enhance participants' competence in leading within complex and dynamic systems. DrPH students only.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Communicating for Public Health Impact
courses.description: This course is one of a series of leadership courses in the executive DrPH. Its purpose is to help students to better understand and apply skills and approaches to use a variety of channels to communicate public health science to diverse stakeholders to positively influence health behavior and public health policies.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Program Evaluation for Health Leaders
courses.description: This is one of a series of research courses in the Executive DrPH. Its purpose is to help students understand the purposes, types, and value of evaluation and how they might use it in their work.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Leadership for Effective Implementation
courses.description: This class will provide students with an opportunity to learn about implementation science and to understand the complementarity of implementation science and intervention science in improving population outcomes. Students will gain an understanding of the importance of implementation science for addressing public health concerns and the role implementation science can play in bringing public health practice and research closer together. Students will develop an understanding of implementation science frameworks and approaches.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Cultural Competence for 21st Century Health Leaders
courses.description: We will examine the ways in which culture and cultural competency intersects with health, and how public health efforts can benefit by understanding relationships between culture and health.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Systems Thinking and Collective Impact
courses.description: This course is designed to help you become familiar with and thoughtfully apply a variety of practical, structured systems thinking approaches to improve care, service delivery systems, policy, and/or environments in which we live. We'll use these methods to both understand individuals' experiences as the foundation for driving change as well as to ''zoom out'' and see the broader system around a population health challenge.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Quality Improvement
courses.description: Provides an introduction and overview of quality improvement efforts in health care. Explores the evidence for why quality improvements are needed, measurements of how health care quality is determined as well as how to implement and manage successful quality improvement techniques. DrPH students only.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Managing the Healthcare Workforce
courses.description: Workforce issues play a central role in virtually all organizational problems and challenges. At times, workforce issues may be the primary cause of a problem, while in other cases, they may be one of several underlying causes. Similarly, it is difficult to identify a solution to an organizational problem that does not involve some aspect of workforce management. DrPH students only.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Program Planning and Design
courses.description: The course focuses on approaches to planning programs that promote individual and community health. It will enable students to understand the essential steps in the program planning process, needs assessments, establishing goals and objectives, and selecting and developing program strategies. The course offers a unique opportunity for students to design a program that addresses a public health issue of interest and emerging threats in global health. Students will apply their experiences and evidence to develop a program based on a topic identified in the preceding Systems Thinking course, HPM 966 , or any other area they would like to consider.
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit; may be repeated in the same term for different topics.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Training and Pedagogy for Health Leaders
courses.description: In this class you will learn how to apply best pedagogical practices to develop effective educational experiences that meet learning needs of audiences in academic, organizational, and community settings. DrPH students only.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Program Planning, Implementation and Evaluation
courses.description: The course focuses on approaches to program planning, implementation, and evaluation that promote individual and community health. It will enable students to understand the essential steps in the program planning and implementation process, including 1) needs assessment, 2) establishing program goals and objectives, 3) selecting and developing program and implementation strategies, and 4) evaluating process, outcomes, and impact. Students will be introduced to evidence-based approaches to promote effective program implementation and evaluation. Attention to cultural humility and contextual adaptations will be integrated throughout the course. Students will learn and apply relevant frameworks and tools through course assignments.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Master's (Non-Thesis)
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.

courses.subject: HPM
courses.title: Doctoral Research and Dissertation
courses.repeat_rules: May be repeated for credit.
